newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy railway workers step up strike plans.
newsitem.headline: Italy railway workers step up strike plans.

text.p: Talks between Italian state railway and its workers over contracts broke down on Tuesday and union leaders said they would now extend a planned strike next month and call a nationwide strike in January.

A spokesman for the transport workers union FILT said talks broke down after less than three hours. Leaders from Italy's three main trades union confederations consequently decided to extend a planned stoppage on December 13 to eight hours from four hours and to call a national rail strike on January 12.

The industrial action planned for December was part of a wider protest by industrial and transport workers in sympathy with metalworkers, who have staged two strikes in the last two months over a failure to renew their contracts.
Italy's 125,000 rail workers are also protesting a failure to renew their contracts, which expired on December 31, 1995.
No one at the railway company was immediately available for comment.
The FILT spokesman said January's planned action was scheduled not to disrupt a planned Christmas and New Year "truce" between unions and employers.
The spokesman quoted FILT National Secretary Dino Testa as saying Italy's railways were in a "critical situation" and that the company was planning to cut back services and staff.

He complained that new Ferrovie managing director Giancarlo Cimoli did not attend Tuesday's meeting or one on November 21. Cimoli took over at the helm of the company last month after his predecessor Lorenzo Necci was arrested in a corruption probe.
